acceptance: Red first: a test with an inline source of an empty Test function makes emptytests.Check fail and name file, line and function; a body with t.Skip(reason) passes; a parse error fails the scan.
The build handoff floor and the ship repo-contract pack run the guard, proven by a test through the real floor entry that refuses a lane diff adding an empty test.
The guard reports 0 offenders on main.
100% coverage on each changed function, zero code comments, and the package note docs/architecture/packages/internal-emptytests.md in STE.
fix: Rebuild the cl-c13 work as a new linear branch from origin/main: go/internal/emptytests (Scan skips vendor, testdata, dot and underscore directories; a parse error fails the guard; a qualifying Test, Fuzz or Benchmark function with zero statements offends; t.Skip with a reason passes), a gate registry seed in the rawgitratchet pattern, and the repo-contract pack entry so the build handoff floor and ship run it. Reuse gotestname for the ignored-directory rule if it holds that rule, so the rule keeps one home.
summary: ADR-0158 decision 19 asks for a guard against vacuous tests: in cycle 2035 empty test bodies such as func TestX(t *testing.T) {} passed every audit (docs/research/cost-aware-repair-2026-10.md F1.9, F1.10). No deterministic gate states the rule. acsnames only checks that a named test exists, so an empty test satisfies it. An earlier console build (uncommitted, worktree dev/cl-c13 on base 16bf6ff08) wrote the library go/internal/emptytests, a gate registry seed and repo-contract wiring, with a design in dev/cl-c13/DESIGN.md. Main has 0 offenders outside testdata today.
title: A gate refuses a Go test, fuzz or benchmark function with an empty body
